options.text: Earth is at a distance where temperatures allow water to stay liquid.
Earth is the largest planet, so it can hold more water.
Any distance from the Sun would still keep water liquid on Earth.
Earth is the fastest planet, so its water never freezes.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Jhanvi builds a simple Solar System model. Her teacher asks why Earth's distance from the Sun matters for liquid water and for life.

part_answers.answer: Earth's orbital distance keeps a temperature range where liquid water can exist, which supports habitability.

teacher.key_rationale: Earth's distance from the Sun sets a temperature range that allows liquid water. Size or orbital speed alone, or claiming any distance works, miss that position-to-habitability link.
